articles.title: No obvious sector to buy? So try an unconventional way: 7 stocks from different sectors with upside potential of up to 26%
articles.description: So, what to do if you cannot pick a sector to buy into? Forget about themes and waves, and go looking directly for individual businesses that are strong. In a market with no clear leadership, the winners will not all come from one sector. They will be scattered, one strong company here, another there, across different parts of the market. But this raises a hard question. If you are not using a sector as your guide, how do you find these strong individual businesses? What do you look for? This is where an unconventional approach helps.

articles.title: An algorithm off switch isn’t enough. Big tech needs a duty of care over addictive designs | Zoe Daniel
articles.description: As AI advances minute by minute and governments grapple with new developments they don’t know how to manage, holding big tech accountable becomes even more urgent A digital duty of care is about a lot more than opting out of “the algorithm”. And after the simplistic and at best patchy exercise of the under-16s social media ban, we shouldn’t let the government get away with another populist policy that looks good on the surface but doesn’t get to the core of the problem. A digital duty of care must hold the tech bros accountable for the safety of the spaces that they have created. Continue reading...

articles.title: Areca, coconut prices
Mary Kathleen’s uranium town still had 212 homes when its mine closed in 1982; the company settlement was dismantled and auctioned off in 1983
articles.description: Mary Kathleen was once a thriving community centered around a uranium mine in Queensland, complete with schools, a cinema, and numerous homes. Following the mine's closure in 1982, the town was meticulously dismantled, with houses moved to other locations, leaving only remnants of foundations and streets. Today, the area has been transformed into a popular tourist destination, featuring a rehabilitated mine that tells its unique history.

articles.title: A Nigerian engineer built his first model house with 14,800 sand-filled plastic bottles; the experiment later grew into 15 houses, including a five-bedroom duplex

The project addresses plastic waste while offering an affordable housing solution.
